newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Waterford Foods sees lower 1996 profits.
newsitem.headline: Waterford Foods sees lower 1996 profits.

text.p: Irish food group Waterford Foods plc said on Tuesday it expected 1996 pretax profits to be below current market expectations but not less than 19.7 million Irish pounds.
The group said diificult trading conditions which confronted the group last year had continued but said trading conditions would improve in 1997.
"Trading conditions in 1997 will improve following a restoration of the balance between raw material costs and market returns which has recently been achieved," Waterford said in a statement.

The group said its interim results for the half-year ended June 30, 1996, had referred to difficult trading conditions which had confronted it at that time, including a severe imbalance between raw material prices and market returns.
"These conditions persisted for the remainder of 1996. In addition, other difficulties adversely impacted some of the group's operations in the final quarter," it said.
Waterford said these difficulties included highly competitive conditions in the Dublin liquid milk market which co-incided with delays in the completion of the Premier rationalisation programme.

It said volumes were also lower than anticipated in the UK juice business while the strength of sterling heightened competition from continental manufacturers in the UK mozzarella market, impacting prices in the final quarter.
"Accordingly, 1996 profits will be below current market expectations," Waterford said.
